chapter: Tiny Kahn, radio and Your Show of Shows
title: Stan Fishelson and hearing the Second Herd live
summary: Mandel recalls meeting trumpeter Stan Fishelson in the Borscht Belt around 1941, praises his lead playing, and says Fishelson became a contractor.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Was Bernie Glow or Stan Fishelson playing most of the lead trumpet?

They split it, Stan Fishelson was a marvelous trumpet player, he was the best in his day, as a lead, like a pure lead sound, like that’s the guy you hear on top in, “Early Autumn,” for instance, just a wonderful concept. He’s a guy I ran into in the mountains – I forgot to mention that whole thing, before I was ever with Venuti, when I was a junior in high school, I’d spend my summer vacations working in the Borscht Belt, playing up at the summer hotels and I first ran into Stan Fischelson up there, he was 16 and I was about 14. So I was really playing professionally from about 1942 or ‘41.
Stan died pretty young didn’t he?

Yeah, he became a big contractor in town here and before that in New York too. He sort of gave up, didn’t give up playing the trumpet, he kept playing all his life but he really… from about the early 50s he started to lose his chops somewhat and just wasn't the trumpet player he was back in the 40s when he was such a giant. I think his interest focused more into the business end of the business and he was very good at what he did.
Because Bernie Glow became the king of the New York lead trumpet players.
That’s right, Stan went into theaters see. Stan followed the money… and that’s not a put down, that’s just you know…
No, it’s what he chose to do.
It’s what he chose to do, that’s all, but what a trumpet player.
How much did you hear that band live, the Second Herd?

As much as I could. I never heard a band that was that good. Except in their own ways certain Basie bands and certain Ellington bands, but I’d say those three rank up there. I never heard Lunceford in their prime so I can’t really say.
